Thank you so much for watering my plants
while I was away. It was a real relief to
know they were in such good hands.
I came home to green leaves and happy
soil, and I truly appreciate it.

If there is ever anything I can do for
you, please just let me know. I owe you
one, and a coffee on me is the least I
can do.

label: physics homework
prompt: forces on a block on an incline — free body diagram with worked solution
reply: Drew the incline free-body diagram and worked the solution.

plan.request: forces on a block on an incline with worked solution

blocks.prompt: Free-body diagram of a 10 kg block resting on a smooth-looking inclined plane at 30 degrees to the horizontal. Draw the incline as a sloped line rising to the right with the angle 30 degrees marked at the bottom, and draw the block as a small square sitting on the slope. Draw three labelled arrows from the block's center: a long arrow straight down labelled 'gravity mg = 98 N (10 kg x 9.8)', an arrow perpendicular to the slope pointing away from it labelled 'normal force N', and an arrow pointing up the slope labelled 'friction f = mu N (mu = 0.2)'. Label the axes parallel and perpendicular to the slope. Keep labels short and legible.

spec.plan: Page 138x60 plain. Incline: surface line rising to right at 30 deg. Block (10 kg) rests on surface; block tool places it. Forces from block: weight straight down (gravity mg=98 N), normal perpendicular to surface, friction up the slope (opposing downhill tendency; user specified up the slope). Angle mark 30 deg at bottom-left of incline. Axes labels: parallel and perpendicular to slope, placed near the block. Surface from (12,48) to (95,48) is flat base; incline should be a sloped line: use surface on=[[20,50],[110,50]]? Keep it simple: surface line from (14,50) to (120,50) would be flat; instead the incline is a sloped line rising right: block sits on a ramp line from (14,52) to (118,52-? ) with slope tan30=0.577. Use ramp from (10,54) to (120,54-110*0.577=-9.5) too tall. Use length 80: from (30,52) to (30+80cos30, 52-80 sin30) = (99.3,12). Ramp points: (30,52) -> (99.3,12). Block at=0.5 -> centre about (64.7,32). Force lengths: weight 14 mm, normal 12 mm, friction 10 mm.

blocks.prompt: Step-by-step solution, one line per step, left-aligned, with a short note to the right of each line. Line 1: Perpendicular to slope: N = m g cos(30 degrees) (note: balance perpendicular forces). Line 2: N = 10 x 9.8 x 0.866 = 84.9 N (note: plug in). Line 3: Friction f = mu N = 0.2 x 84.9 = 17.0 N (note: friction opposes motion). Line 4: Along slope: m a = m g sin(30 degrees) - f (note: Newton's second law). Line 5: m g sin(30 degrees) = 10 x 9.8 x 0.5 = 49.0 N (note: gravity component). Line 6: a = (49.0 - 17.0) / 10 = 3.2 m/s^2 (note: divide by mass). Line 7: Check: a is positive so the block slides down the slope at 3.2 m/s^2 (note: check sign).

spec.plan:
Worked solution, 7 lines, left-aligned at x=6. Math size 5 mm, line spacing 2.4*5=12 mm (3.6*5=18 mm for lines with fractions; none here). Notes to the right at x=100, size 3.5 as text.
Line y positions: 12, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72 ... need 7 lines: use spacing 10 mm for fitting in 80 mm height: y = 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70. Keep within 4 mm margin: page 172x80.
